# Setup Guide

How to get from a clean machine to a running game. There are two levels of
setup; pick one.

- **Minimal (text editor):** a terminal, a text editor, and the SDL2 dev
  package. Enough to build, run, and test. **Recommended default.**
- **Rich (IDE):** the same tools plus an IDE for people who want one.

See [`DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md`](DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md) for the full
editor/IDE details, and [`BUILD.md`](BUILD.md) for build troubleshooting.

## 1. Install the toolchain

**Debian / Ubuntu / Linux Mint (primary platform):**

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake git libsdl2-dev
```

**Fedora:** `sudo dnf install -y gcc-c++ make cmake git SDL2-devel`
**macOS:** `brew install cmake sdl2`
**Windows:** use MSYS2 (UCRT64 shell) — see `DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md`.

## 2. Get the source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/FreeOpenSourceSyndicate/FreeOpenSourceSyndicate.git
cd FOSSynd
```

## 3. Build

```bash
./scripts/build.sh
```

This builds the engine-agnostic core, the unit tests, and the SDL2 game target.

## 4. Run

```bash
./build/src/FOSSynd
```

## 5. Test

```bash
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```
